final_codebook.domain: Subtracting fractions and mixed numbers, including denominator alignment, normalization, regrouping, component subtraction, and simplified final answers

skills.name: Find common denominator
skills.definition: Determine a common denominator and rewrite fractional parts as equivalent fractions with that denominator before subtraction.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a step explicitly finds an LCD, LCM, or common denominator for unlike denominators.
Tag when one or both fractions are converted to equivalent fractions to create matching denominators before subtraction.
Tag for pure fractions or fractional parts of mixed numbers when denominator alignment is the main purpose of the step.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when denominators are already the same and no equivalent-fraction conversion is performed.
Do not tag rewriting a whole number as n + 0/d for mixed-number structure; that belongs to normalization/preparation.
Do not tag subtraction, borrowing, or final simplification steps.

skills.name: Normalize subtraction form
skills.definition: Rewrite a quantity into a subtraction-ready mixed-number form, including converting an improper mixed number to standard mixed form or writing a whole number as a whole plus 0 over a denominator.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a mixed number with an improper fractional part is rewritten as an equivalent standard mixed number.
Tag when a whole number is rewritten as n + 0/d to make mixed-number subtraction structurally compatible.
Tag when the step changes representation only to prepare whole and fractional parts for later subtraction.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag equivalent-fraction conversion whose purpose is matching unlike denominators; that is S01.
Do not tag borrowing/regrouping after subtraction has begun; that is S05.
Do not tag final recombination or simplification of the answer.

skills.name: Subtract fraction parts
skills.definition: Subtract fractions that already share a denominator by subtracting numerators and keeping the denominator, including fraction parts within mixed-number subtraction.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when numerators are subtracted over a common denominator.
Tag when fraction parts of mixed numbers are subtracted after denominators are already aligned or unchanged.
Tag whether the immediate fraction result is positive, zero, or negative before any borrowing adjustment.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag steps whose main purpose is finding a common denominator or converting equivalent fractions.
Do not tag whole-part subtraction by itself.
Do not tag borrowing/regrouping steps that first adjust the whole and fractional parts.

skills.name: Subtract whole parts
skills.definition: Subtract the whole-number components of mixed numbers or rewritten whole numbers as a separate part of the computation.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a step explicitly subtracts whole parts such as 4 − 3 = 1.
Tag when a whole number is treated as the whole component in mixed-number subtraction.
Tag even if a later borrowing step changes the whole-part result.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag pure fraction-only subtraction with no whole-number component.
Do not tag rewriting a whole number as n + 0/d unless whole-part subtraction is also actually performed in the tagged step.
Do not tag final answer composition that merely states the mixed number.

skills.name: Borrow across whole
skills.definition: Regroup one whole as fractional units to continue subtraction when the fractional part of the minuend is too small.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a step borrows 1 from the whole part and converts it to denominator-based fractional units such as d/d.
Tag when regrouping is used after or in anticipation of a negative fractional difference.
Tag when the borrowed whole is combined with the existing fractional part before completing fraction subtraction.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when subtraction is completed without regrouping.
Do not tag rewriting a whole number as n + 0/d before subtraction begins; that is S02.
Do not tag final combination of the answer after borrowing is complete.

skills.name: Simplify and express
skills.definition: Reduce the computed result to lowest terms when needed and present it in an appropriate final form such as a fraction, mixed number, or integer.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a fraction is reduced to lowest terms.
Tag when 0 over a denominator or a mixed number with 0 fractional part is simplified to a whole number.
Tag when computed whole and fractional parts are combined into the final accepted form.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag the arithmetic subtraction step itself unless the step also explicitly simplifies or formats the final answer.
Do not tag denominator alignment, normalization, or borrowing steps.
Do not tag intermediate component results that are not yet being simplified or expressed as the final answer.

decisions.reasoning: This skill had 3/3 consensus and is clearly independent from subtraction and simplification. It is broadly applicable and diagnostically useful because some items require denominator alignment while others do not.

Both operations are preparatory representation changes that make mixed-number subtraction structurally possible. They are not independently testable in this item set often enough to justify separate skills, and several expert codebooks already bundled them. Merging improves minimality and clarity.

decisions.details: Kept C04 as S03 with refined wording
decisions.reasoning: Subtracting like-denominator fractions is a distinct cognitive operation from finding a common denominator and from whole-part subtraction. It appears in pure-fraction items and mixed-number items, supporting independence and identifiability.

Although only isolated by one expert, whole-part subtraction is independently testable because some mixed-number items require whole-part subtraction alongside no borrowing, and pure fraction items do not. Keeping it separate preserves completeness and better diagnostic resolution than bundling all subtraction into one skill.

decisions.details: Removed C06 after distributing its content across S03 and S04
decisions.reasoning: C06 is a broader bundled skill that combines fraction-part and whole-part subtraction. Because those two operations are independently testable in the dossiers and represent different cognitive actions, keeping C06 would violate non-redundancy and reduce diagnostic precision.

This skill had 3/3 consensus and is a clearly distinct regrouping process, separate from normalization and subtraction. It is essential for completeness because several mixed-number items require borrowing while others do not.

decisions.details: Merged C08 + C09 + C10 into S06
decisions.reasoning: Post-processing steps of simplification and final expression frequently co-occur and are bundled in two expert codebooks. Splitting them would create narrow, low-consensus skills with ambiguous tagging boundaries, while the combined skill remains coherent and easier to annotate consistently.

decisions.details: Refined all retained skills to sharpen inclusion/exclusion boundaries and align examples with dossier evidence
decisions.reasoning: Refinement was needed to ensure independent annotators can distinguish normalization from denominator alignment, subtraction from borrowing, and arithmetic from final-answer processing.

summary: The final codebook consolidates the aligned candidates into exactly six skills by preserving the strongest consensus operations and merging only where the underlying process is genuinely the same or not independently diagnosable in this item set. Common-denominator work, normalization, fraction subtraction, whole-part subtraction, borrowing, and final simplification/expression were retained as the clearest and most diagnostically useful structure.
